title: operator approval hatchery and residency-hold KMS prover
author: Marcus Nguyen
description: Summary: Introduces an operator approval hatchery middleware and a KMS-backed residency-hold prover used by RBAC v2 decisions and audit enrichment. Motivation: customers operating under strict data residency rules requested an auditable operator consent gate that can place a temporary 'residency hold' on requests when the backend is unable to guarantee region pinning (e.g. failover to standby region). This PR adds: 1) operator approval hatchery service: lightweight queue + UI hook that surfaces candidate requests requiring explicit operator consent (with TTL and escalation metadata); 2) residency-hold KMS prover: signs a short-lived residency assertion using tenant-scoped CMKs to prove the request was reviewed and consented by an operator in a permitted jurisdiction; 3) RBAC v2 adapter: conditional role assertion that can require residency-hold or operator-consent claims before certain high-risk actions (eg. export, model-download); 4) audit enrichment: attach signed residency assertions and operator decision metadata to the audit envelope; 5) tests & docs: unit/integration tests, an integration test harness scenario simulating region failover, and a runbook for SREs. Checklist: - [x] design doc (ENG-4021) - [x] policy schema changes with backwards-compatible defaults - [x] operator hatchery service + API - [x] residency-hold prover (KMS signing + verification) - [x] RBAC adapter + decision-mapper - [x] audit envelope enrichment - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] docs and runbook Notes on compatibility and security: The residency-hold assertion is an auditable signed blob (signed by a tenant-scoped CMK) that contains minimal metadata (request id, operator id, timestamp, allowed-regions list, TTL) and a hash of the evaluated policy. Verification logic guards against replay and stale TTLs. We intentionally keep the assertion small to avoid token bloat in the audit path. Backwards compatibility is preserved: existing roles without the new condition continue behaving the same. Default rollout is shadow-mode where the RBAC adapter logs decisions and enrichment but does not block. Implementation highlights and why this differs from previous residency work: - We separate the human approval path (hatchery) from automated consent (policy-driven fallback), making it easier to audit and to surface false positives to operators. - Rather than relying on global operator keys, we use tenant-scoped CMKs and KMS key policy bindings so the signed assertion can be cryptographically traced to the tenant's KMS and later verified by auditors. - The RBAC v2 condition matcher now understands two new claim types: residency_hold and operator_consent, allowing fine-grained rules in policy manifests. Testing and rollout plan: - Start shadow mode on staging for 1 week with simulated region failover - Enable canary (5%) for test tenants, collect alerting for latency and audit envelope size - Roll full enforcement after two weeks and successful regression-free windows Monitoring and alerts: - New metrics: hatchery.queue_depth, hatchery.approval_latency_p50/p95, residency_prover.sign_errors, rbac.residency_hold_denials - Alert: hatchery.queue_depth > 100 for 5m; residency_prover.sign_errors > 1% 10m; audit_envelope_size_p95 increase > 20% Risks & mitigations: - KMS signing rate limits: we batch ephemeral assertions and fallback to pre-authorized operator-countersigned tokens when limits are reached. - Operator abuse: audit trail + HMAC of operator session added to assertion; we also rate-limit approvals per operator. - Token bloat: assertions TTLs default to 15m; admin can tune with policy.
